chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), that he disliked the hunting of the falcon except for that whose slaughter was completed.
ai.seo_question: Is the meat of a hunted falcon halal if it is not slaughtered at the moment of capture?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on hunting with falcons (*bazi*), distinguishing between mere capture and proper ritual slaughter (*dhabh*). He stipulates that the animal is only permissible to eat if the throat is cut and blood drained at the moment of capture, ensuring the act of killing is intentional and valid, rather than relying on the animal dying from exhaustion or impact alone. This ruling reflects the Shia emphasis on the precise conditions of *dhabh* even in the context of animal-assisted hunting.
